title: Startup credit program
description: One verified startup credit, perk or discount program. One file per program at data/programs/<slug>.yml. Every claim must trace to the vendor's own page.

slug.description: Kebab-case identifier. MUST equal the filename without .yml, e.g. cloudflare-for-startups.

company.description: Vendor name as the vendor writes it, e.g. Cloudflare.

program.description: Official program name, e.g. Cloudflare for Startups. Not a description.

category.description: Primary category. Generated from data/categories.yml -- do not invent values.

tags.description: Optional free tags for cross-category discovery, e.g. gpu, vector-db, soc2.

apply_url.description: Where a founder actually applies. No affiliate, referral or utm_* parameters -- CI rejects them. Must be reachable; a cross-domain redirect to a parent brand means the program is likely discontinued.

official_source.description: The EXACT vendor URL carrying the sentence in evidence_quote. Not the prettiest landing page. If the amount lives on a docs or help-centre subpage, link that subpage.

benefit_type.description: What kind of thing this is. credit=a grant of spendable credit. discount=percentage off list. free-plan=a named plan free for a period. usage-allowance=non-dollar units (tokens, characters, seats). matched-credit=vendor matches your spend. spend-commitment=credit unlocked by committing spend. Choosing 'credit' for a discount misrepresents the offer.

benefit_summary.description: One objective sentence. State the structure, not a marketing claim. 'Up to $350k in credits, tiered by funding stage and partner status.' Never 'the best cloud credits program'.

amount_is_published.description: Does the vendor publish a figure at all? Many real programs (MongoDB, Anthropic, Modal, Snowflake) publish none. false means 'vendor states no number', which is different from 'we did not look'.

amount_max.description: Maximum headline value in `currency`. Only when the vendor publishes it. Never estimate, round, or convert. Must be null when verification_level is needs-manual-verification.

currency.description: Currency the vendor publishes in. OVHcloud and Scaleway publish EUR -- do not silently convert to USD.

duration_months.description: How long the benefit lasts. A $100k/12-month offer is not the same product as $100k/24-month.

expiry_note.description: Expiry or burn-down terms in the vendor's words, e.g. 'valid for up to one year or when all credits are consumed, whichever comes first'.

after_credits.description: What happens when the benefit ends. Affects runway planning: Algolia auto-transitions to pay-as-you-go; Retool drops to 25% off in year two.

excludes.description: What the credit cannot be spent on. Civo excludes GPU instances; Retool excludes Enterprise and all annual plans.

stacking_notes.description: Stated non-combination rules. Sentry: YC and a16z founders must use their portal deal instead, and it does not combine. Vanta voids if you are already engaged with sales.

tiers.description: Only for genuinely tiered programs. Per-tier eligibility is REQUIRED here: advertising a $350k headline while omitting that the top tier needs $5M raised shows founders a number they can never reach.

name.description: Tier name as the vendor writes it.

quote.description: Shortest exact span from the vendor page describing this tier.

funding_required.description: TRI-STATE. false ONLY when the vendor affirmatively says you need not have raised. unknown (or omitted) means we did not confirm -- and NEVER qualifies the entry for the 'No Funding Required' collection.

accelerator_required.description: TRI-STATE. false ONLY when the vendor affirmatively says no accelerator, VC or partner referral is needed. unknown never qualifies for 'No Partner or Accelerator Required'.

open_to_bootstrapped.description: TRI-STATE. true ONLY when the page affirmatively says bootstrapped or self-funded companies qualify. Absence of an exclusion is not permission.

requires_vc_backing.description: TRI-STATE. true when institutional funding is a stated condition, as with Anthropic's credit tier.

partner_gate.description: Not a boolean. none=open. improves-offer=better terms via a partner but not required (Miro: $500 solo vs $1,000 with a partner). required-soft=practically needs an intro. required-hard=needs a partner code. tiered=varies by tier (Cloudflare).

partners.description: Named accelerators/VCs that unlock or improve the offer. 'accelerator_required: true' alone is not actionable for a founder.

partners_url.description: Vendor's own partner list, when it publishes one rather than enumerating.

funding_min_usd.description: Numeric FLOOR when one exists. Deel requires at least $500k raised; Modal at least $1M. A max-only model renders a floor identically to a ceiling and silently misleads bootstrapped founders.

funding_max_usd.description: Numeric ceiling on total funding raised.

stages.description: Stages the vendor states it serves.

company_age_max_years.description: Maximum company age. Pair with age_basis -- vendors measure from different events.

age_basis.description: What company_age_max_years is measured from. Clerk measures from LAUNCH, not incorporation.

employees_max.description: Headcount cap. Amplitude <20, Intercom <15, Miro <30, Linear <50, Notion <100, Zendesk <250.

revenue_max_usd.description: Revenue cap. Help Scout gates on <$1M ARR -- a rule no funding field can express.

new_customer_only.description: TRI-STATE. Near-universal and a top rejection cause. Railway required under $100 lifetime spend; Cloudflare is first-time applicants only.

requires_incorporation.description: TRI-STATE. Whether a registered legal entity is required.

requires_company_email.description: TRI-STATE. Whether a matching business-domain email is required to apply.

regions.description: Where the vendor says the program is available. Use 'global' ONLY when the vendor says worldwide/global. Use a lowercase group id (e.g. apac) only when the vendor itself used that regional wording -- and then regions_basis must be 'inferred' unless the vendor also enumerated the countries. Region groups are a display aid and are NEVER proof a given country qualifies.

excluded_regions.description: Countries or regions the vendor explicitly excludes (sanctions, export controls, unsupported billing).

regions_basis.description: THE HONESTY GATE for country pages. asserted=vendor named the country, said worldwide/global, or named a region AND enumerated its countries -> may appear as Confirmed. inferred=vendor named a region but not its countries (a bare 'APAC') -> Not confirmed. unstated=vendor published no geographic restriction -> Not confirmed. Most real programs are 'unstated'.

regions_quote.description: Shortest exact span supporting regions_basis: asserted. Required in spirit whenever you claim 'asserted'.

eligibility_notes.description: Anything structured fields cannot hold. For partially-verified entries, name exactly which detail could not be inspected.

application_mechanism.description: How you actually apply. The difference between an afternoon and a quarter.

requires_sales_call.description: TRI-STATE. Plain and Crisp have no self-serve path at all.

approval_time.description: Vendor-published turnaround, e.g. '2-3 business days'. Only when published.

obligations.description: Non-monetary conditions. Grafana and Vultr require agreeing to be a public reference customer. These are real costs and belong beside the benefit.

status.description: Current state. 'no-program' records a vendor that explicitly states it offers no startup credits -- a genuinely useful negative. An entry whose only live artifact is a dated changelog or blog post may NEVER be marked active.

status_basis.description: asserted=the status is quoted from the page (fill status_quote). inferred=your reading. Restrictive statuses invented by a reviewer harm founders as much as missing ones.

status_quote.description: Shortest exact span supporting a restrictive status.

discontinued_date.description: ISO date the program closed, when known. Webflow closed 2026-06-30 and is still listed as live by most aggregators -- dated closures are among the highest-value records here.

replaced_by.description: What superseded a discontinued program, if anything.

last_verified.description: The date a HUMAN opened official_source and confirmed these terms. Never set by a bot, never backfilled. Re-verification cycle is 180 days.

verified_by.description: GitHub handle of the person who did that.

verification_level.description: verified=the official page or docs were opened and the claim directly confirmed; carries evidence_quote. partially-verified=official info was read but some detail could not be inspected; name it in eligibility_notes. needs-manual-verification=the page is blocked, gated or account-only; NO financial amount may be published. A search snippet never carries the same standing as a page someone opened.

evidence_quote.description: The SHORTEST exact span from official_source that supports the claim. Never a paragraph or a full FAQ answer. Required for verified and partially-verified; omit for needs-manual-verification.

conflicting_sources.description: When a vendor contradicts ITSELF, record both readings rather than silently picking one. Algolia's page says <7yr/<$15M while its own FAQ says <3yr/<$5M. Picking the generous one misleads founders about rejection risk and makes good-faith reporters think the entry is fabricated.

bot_blocked.description: Vendor 403s or JS-renders, so automated checking cannot see the page. Permanent manual-review flag. Around 15% of vendors -- Google Cloud, Oracle, Carta, Cohere, JetBrains. Flag once; stop re-triaging.

last_checked.description: BOT-written: the last automated liveness check. Deliberately separate from last_verified. A bot fetching a URL is not a human confirming a $100k offer still exists on those terms.

related.description: Slugs of related entries. Use for shared credit pools: Neon and Databricks advertise the SAME $200k through one form, so listing both without linking them double-counts.

fetch_note.description: What happened when the page was last fetched: 200 and rendered, 403, JS-only shell, redirected, 404. Recorded so a later reviewer knows whether a gap was the vendor blocking us or nobody looking.
